cells.tense: Right now you are in it, and the connection is running, not waiting.
cells.ask: Tell the person you are moving with which part of this direction is yours to hold, then hold it today without checking in about it.
cells.core:
You can tell a pull that belongs to you from one you borrowed, and you do it in small choices — who you move toward, what you drop. That is what lets two streams meet and stay one flow instead of two people agreeing to want the same thing.

It is going well right now. You are not testing it and not talking it to death; you are in it with someone, choosing the same direction on purpose. What keeps it here is that the choice stays spoken and the weight stays divided. When it does, the connection has substance without either of you carrying all of it, and it can be fed more of the same.
cells.sheetLine: You know which way this is going. Say it once, out loud.
cells.verb: flowing two streams into one chosen direction

cells.tense: You are already living at a point ahead of where this connection actually stands.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been deciding ahead of the other person. Leave it undecided today, and let them bring their half tomorrow instead of you bringing both.
cells.core:
You're steering both halves before the other person has moved. Some version of where this lands exists in your head — how it should go, what it will mean, who you will both be on the other side — and you are already arranging the present around it. The arranging is doing the work the meeting was supposed to do.

When two streams are already one in your planning, there's nothing left for the other person to bring. What holds it together isn't vision. It's the same care you're already giving, without the grip — the kind that lets a thing grow because you stopped pulling it toward a shape. Release one decision and let it land on its own.

cells.tense: You are standing outside a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what you want, plainly, to someone who will just hear it. No case, no apology. Then stop and let it stand.
cells.core:
Running well, this looks like plainness. You feel a direction, you say it in ordinary words, and the saying does not need defending or checking. The pull gets followed without asking permission first.

That is not where you are. You feel it and you are not following it. Now the days go by and you call the direction someone else's problem, or a phase you are past, or a thing you will get to. What is absent is the plain knowing that survives being said out loud. You do not have to be sure. Let one piece of it land where you cannot take it back.

cells.tense: The pen is already moving in a room you have not said you are writing in.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did this week that was your direction moving, and tell one person you did it. Not what it helped. Just that it was yours.
cells.core:
Running well, you are shaping what holds without any fuss about it. You notice what you are drawn toward, you follow it openly, and the people around you can see the direction is yours, not the situation's.

That is not the shape it's taking. You are already shaping which connections last and which drift, by what you give attention to and what you let fall away. But you describe it as if the situation were deciding itself, or as if you were just going along with what is obviously right. The doing is happening. The saying so is not. Claiming a want started to feel like too much, so it got folded into practical language and nobody credited you with it, including you.
